hero.title: More control. Less overhead.
hero.lede: Version 0.2.0 brings isolation, exact authorization, pluggable I/O, auditing, and telemetry. Your agents can do useful work while a separate broker keeps every outside action on a short leash.

highlights.title: Build complete plans without tool sprawl.
highlights.body: The model gets one familiar scripting tool. It can discover and combine only the capabilities you allow.
points: Loops, functions, pipelines, here-docs, and real jq
No processes, files, sockets, or inherited environment
Hard limits on time, memory, output, recursion, and calls

highlights.title: Approve every outside action.
highlights.body: A separate local broker verifies the caller, checks an exact rule, applies I/O limits, and approves one use.
points: Deny by default for each agent, capability, and provider
Limits for destination, method, calls, bytes, and time

highlights.title: See what happened from end to end.
highlights.body: Audit records show what was approved. Traces show how the run flowed. Logs keep costs, refusals, errors, and optional transcripts.
points: One trace across runner, broker, and provider
Standard OpenTelemetry over HTTP or gRPC, tested with OpenObserve

changes.title: Every provider call starts clean.
changes.body: Pure local providers get no host access. Networked providers get one narrow Dekopon HTTP interface. Every call starts in a fresh Wasm sandbox with its own memory, time, input, output, and fuel limits.

changes.title: The agent cannot approve itself.
changes.body: The runner sends one limited request over a private local socket. The broker gets identity from the operating system and your config. The model cannot provide its own identity, policy, permission, or runtime limits.

changes.title: Every decision stays tied to its result.
changes.body: The broker records each decision, safe request details, and the final outcome in a hash-linked file. Clear failure codes tell you whether work never started or may have happened without a final audit record.

changes.title: Follow one run across every process.
changes.body: See model turns, scripts, permission checks, provider work, and safe HTTP details in one trace. Keep token use, costs, refusals, errors, and optional transcripts as searchable logs.

telemetry.title: for the current Dekopon sample
telemetry.body: On the project Raspberry Pi, the current OpenObserve sample uses 148 KiB for traces and 52 KiB for logs. The full stream tree uses 1.22 MiB, including other streams, indexes, and metadata.
telemetry.note: Measured 16 August 2026 using physical blocks on disk. This is an aggregate sample, not a fixed cost per prompt.

packages.name: dekopon
packages.body: Check configuration, inspect your agents, and manage isolated model login.

packages.name: dekopon-run
packages.body: Talk to the model, run the one-tool sandbox, and send limited requests to the broker.

packages.body: Verify local identity, check permissions, limit network access, and keep the audit trail.

current: A private local broker that verifies the caller’s operating-system identity
Pure local providers and separately permissioned network providers
One sandboxed model tool with limits for the whole session
Exact allow/deny rules, replay protection, limited HTTP, and durable audit
Local Chrome traces plus standard OpenTelemetry traces and logs
next: Broker-managed provider credentials tied to approved destinations
Signed or remote copies of audit checkpoints
A long-running agent service connected to operator config
Multi-host, multi-tenant networking and production hardening

previous.title: The local foundation
previous.body: Version 0.1 introduced strict agent config, predictable CLI output, model clients, isolated account state, and pure Wasm providers. Version 0.2 adds secure execution, permissioned I/O, auditing, and telemetry.
